title: 861. Prime Palindrome

examples.explanation: 11 is the first prime palindrome at or above 8.
101 is the first prime palindrome at or above 13.

hints: Even-length palindromes beyond 11 are all multiples of 11, so only the number 11 matters among them.
It is enough to build palindromes by mirroring the first half; generate odd-length candidates in increasing order plus the special 11.
Test primality by trial division up to the square root, skipping even divisors after 2.
